question: Which calls did Alastair McCrae take part in, and how did each go?

resolution.read_instruction: Identify whether Alastair McCrae takes part in this call (as OrbitFlow staff or as a prospect/customer participant) and, if so, summarise how the call went: the outcome, next steps, objections raised, and any commitments or decisions made. If he does not appear in the call, report that it does not contain him.
assumptions: No specific call type or company is named, so the search covers all calls in the catalogue.
Speaker identity is taken from the transcript; 'Alastair McCrae' is treated as a person name, not a company.

findings.speaker: Alastair McCrae
findings.quote: Hi hi hi. Imogen? Ben? Can you hear me?
findings.context: Alastair McCrae participated in CALL-006 (Fable Media discovery, 2026-07-09) as the OrbitFlow Account Executive, leading the call. — Participant list and his opening turn; he is the vendor side of this call.

findings.speaker: Imogen Price
findings.quote: Price and complexity are the two risks. And honestly, we may well decide that Zapier plus better process discipline is good enough
findings.context: Outcome was not a close: the prospect said they are interested but not ready to commit, and may choose Zapier plus process discipline instead. Price and complexity were named as the two risks. — Customer's closing summary; the call ended without a decision.

findings.speaker: Imogen Price
findings.quote: I can sign software contracts up to twenty thousand. Above that the founder approves it.
findings.context: Price objection: the Growth package at 1,800 a month (about 21,500 a year) exceeds the customer's budget; she cannot sign software contracts above 20,000 without the founder's approval. — Pricing discussion; she asked about monthly billing and fewer seats (10 instead of 30).

findings.speaker: Alastair McCrae
findings.quote: I'll check with my manager and come back.
findings.context: Alastair committed to check whether monthly billing is available and to come back; he was not sure and had to ask his manager. — Open commitment at end of call.

findings.speaker: Alastair McCrae
findings.quote: Yeah, I can do a Loom.
findings.context: Alastair committed to send a recorded Loom demo tailored to Fable's use case by end of the week, plus the DPA on model training and a customer reference. — Next steps agreed on the call.

findings.speaker: Alastair McCrae
findings.quote: I'm fairly sure it's all plans. But yeah, I'll confirm.
findings.context: Alastair claimed SSO is included on all plans; the customer said other vendors gated it to enterprise, and Alastair was not fully certain and agreed to confirm. — Unresolved claim the customer asked him to verify.

findings.speaker: Alastair McCrae
findings.quote: I'd want to check with an SE, honestly.
findings.context: Alastair's claims about the onboarding ROI, the reference customer's renewal, and the date-alert workflow were not verified; he said he would need to check with an SE and had moved off the reference account. — Several answers were hedged or unverified, which weakened credibility with the prospect.

findings.speaker: Imogen Price
findings.quote: Well. Let's see.
findings.context: Tone was cautious and mixed: the prospect was engaged but skeptical, and the call ended with 'Let's see' rather than commitment. — Inferred from the customer's closing remarks.

findings.speaker: Alastair McCrae
findings.quote: Is there a version where we look at the pricing? Because I could go and —
findings.context: Alastair tried to revisit pricing to retain the customer, and the customer refused, saying a lower price now would imply overcharging earlier. — Save attempt by Alastair; customer rejected it, and the call's framing is that this is not a save call.

findings.speaker: Hazel Wren
findings.quote: If you can do it for eight thousand now, that tells me you could have done it for eight thousand two years ago, and then I'd be quite cross.
findings.context: Customer rejected the pricing offer: if an eight thousand price is available now, it could have been offered two years ago. — Customer's response to Alastair's pricing attempt.

findings.speaker: Alastair McCrae
findings.quote: I probably should have pushed harder on whether you had the capacity for the roadmap we talked about.
findings.context: Alastair acknowledged that during the sale both he and the customer were enthusiastic about a roadmap, and that he should have checked whether the customer had capacity to deliver it. — Alastair takes partial responsibility for the over-purchase; a self-critical statement.

findings.speaker: Hazel Wren
findings.quote: I don't think you did anything wrong. You sold me a good product that does what it says.
findings.context: Customer said Alastair did not do anything wrong: he sold a good product, and she bought more than she needed. — Customer absolves Alastair after his self-criticism.

findings.speaker: Alastair McCrae
findings.quote: I did say that.
findings.context: Alastair confirmed in the sales process that no smaller plan than Growth existed, and that Growth was the entry point. — Customer had asked for a smaller tier; Alastair confirmed none existed at the time of sale.

findings.speaker: Alastair McCrae
findings.quote: None at all. Good luck with the compliance one.
findings.context: Call closed on good terms with no escalation or save; Alastair wished the customer well and the customer said there were no hard feelings. — Final exchange; tone is cordial and the churn is final.

findings.speaker: Alastair McCrae
findings.quote: Yvonne, hi, it's Alastair calling from OrbitFlow, how are you today?
findings.context: Alastair McCrae took part in CALL-019 (Trafford Dental Group, cold call, 2026-09-29) as the OrbitFlow Account Executive. — Participant list names Alastair McCrae as Account Executive, OrbitFlow; he speaks as vendor throughout.

findings.speaker: Yvonne Deeks
findings.quote: Eighteen hundred a month is not a number that exists in my world.
findings.context: The call ended without a sale: the prospect said OrbitFlow was not a fit, mainly because of price (entry package from £1,800/month, versus a budget of roughly two or three hundred a month) and because the stated problem (dental nurse recruitment) is not one OrbitFlow solves. — Outcome of the cold call; the prospect's objection was price and lack of relevance, not a timing issue.

findings.speaker: Alastair McCrae
findings.quote: our entry package starts at eighteen hundred a month.
findings.context: Alastair quoted an entry package starting at eighteen hundred a month, for up to thirty users. — Pricing given by the vendor when asked about cost; the prospect reacted that her practice management software costs less for the whole group.

findings.speaker: Alastair McCrae
findings.quote: I'd have to check.
findings.context: Alastair could not confirm whether NHS e-Referral has an API, and did not commit to an integration. — Prospect raised NHS e-Referral integration; vendor claimed integration with anything with an API but then said he would have to check.

findings.speaker: Yvonne Deeks
findings.quote: I'll be honest with you, I won't read it.
findings.context: Alastair agreed to send information, which the prospect said she would not read; no meeting or follow-up was agreed. The prospect also said she did not want repeated follow-ups. — Next step offered by vendor; prospect declined to engage with it.

findings.speaker: Yvonne Deeks
findings.quote: you haven't asked me a single question about what we actually do.
findings.context: Alastair pitched without first researching the prospect's actual operations, and the prospect said this was the main reason the call went badly; she said a true, specific insight about dental groups would have improved it. — Prospect's critique of the vendor's approach; the vendor acknowledged it ('yeah, fair').

findings.speaker: Yvonne Deeks
findings.quote: and you'd still probably have got a no because of the price.
findings.context: Alastair asked for feedback on what would have changed the outcome and was told the call would have gone better with a true, specific insight; the prospect said she would still likely have said no because of price. — Vendor sought honest feedback at the end of the call.

findings.speaker: Alastair McCrae
findings.quote: Thanks for being straight with me. Most people just hang up.
findings.context: The call's outcome is a clear loss; the prospect was polite but firm, and the vendor's closing ('thanks for being straight with me') suggests no further action planned. — Inferred from the closing exchange; no commitment to follow up was made.

claims.text: CALL-006 Fable Media (prospect discovery, 2026-07-09): Alastair led as OrbitFlow Account Executive; it was not a close. COO Imogen Price said they are interested but not ready to commit, named price and complexity as risks, and said they may choose Zapier plus process discipline. The tone appears cautious and mixed (inferred), ending with 'Let's see'.

On Fable Media, the Growth package at 1,800 a month (about 21,500 a year) exceeds Price's 20,000 signing limit, above which the founder must approve. Alastair's answers were hedged or unverified (onboarding ROI, reference renewal, date-alert workflow; he would check with an SE), and he was unsure about SSO on all plans, which the customer said other vendors gate to enterprise. This weakened credibility.

Alastair's open commitments on Fable Media: send a tailored Loom demo by end of week plus the DPA on model training and a customer reference; check monthly billing with his manager and come back; confirm SSO.

CALL-015 Oakhill Property (churn post-mortem): Alastair tried to revisit pricing to retain the customer, and Operations Director Hazel Wren refused, saying an eight thousand price now implies it could have been offered two years earlier and she would be cross. He confirmed no plan smaller than Growth existed at sale.

On Oakhill, Alastair admitted he should have pushed harder on whether they had capacity for the roadmap; Wren said he did nothing wrong, he sold a good product and she bought more than needed. The call closed cordially with no hard feelings, no escalation or save, and the churn final.

CALL-019 Trafford Dental Group (cold call, 2026-09-29): Alastair quoted an entry package from 1,800 a month for up to 30 users. Yvonne Deeks said it was not a fit, mainly on price (budget roughly two or three hundred a month) and because dental nurse recruitment is not a problem OrbitFlow solves.

On Trafford, Alastair could not confirm whether NHS e-Referral has an API and made no integration commitment. Deeks said he had not asked about her operations, which she called the main reason the call went badly; a true, specific insight would have helped, though she would likely still have said no on price. She said she would not read information he sent, no follow-up was agreed, and she did not want repeated follow-ups.
The Trafford call appears to be a clear loss (inferred): Deeks was polite but firm, and Alastair closed with 'thanks for being straight with me', suggesting no further action.
